item.title: China Coast Guard completes 45-day fisheries patrol in North Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- A China Coast Guard (CCG) fleet has completed a 45-day fisheries law-enforcement patrol on the high seas of the North Pacific, the CCG said Wednesday. The fleet, consisting of two CCG vessels, returned to port Wednesday after completing the patrol mission, the 11th of its kind, the CCG said in a statement. The patrol was conducted under relevant United Nations General Assembly resolution and international conventions, the CCG statement said. In recent years, the CCG has actively implemented relevant UN General Assembly resolution and international conventions. It has conducted boarding and inspection operations on the high seas to crack down on illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing activities, contributing to maintaining order in high seas fisheries and promoting the sustainable development of fishery resources. During the mission, the fleet strengthened oversight of fishing operations and verified vessel registration information, observing and recording 95 fishing vessels from various countries and boarding 20 for inspections, the statement said. The fleet also conducted seven helicopter flights for high-seas law enforcement. The CCG said it would continue to conduct fisheries law-enforcement patrols on the high seas, fulfill its obligations under relevant conventions and help maintain orderly fishing operations in international waters. With sound legislation, strict enforcement and rigorous judicial oversight, China has ranked among the top in compliance assessments of regional fisheries management organizations. At a press briefing in July, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said China stands ready to work with all parties to improve global fisheries governance, uphold international maritime order, and contribute to conservation and sustainable use of marine resources through concrete actions.

item.title: Xi extends congratulations over DPRK's 78th founding anniversary
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and Chinese president, on Wednesday extended congratulations to Kim Jong Un, general secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea (WPK) and president of the State Affairs of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), over the DPRK's 78th founding anniversary. In his message, Xi pointed out that over the past 78 years, under the leadership of the WPK, the DPRK people have achieved vigorous development in various fields of socialist construction through self-reliance, unity and hard work. In recent years in particular, under the leadership of Kim, the WPK and the DPRK people have made every effort to advance economic and social development, scoring a series of development achievements to China's heartfelt delight, said Xi. Xi expressed confidence that the brotherly DPRK people will surely achieve the goals and tasks set forth at the Ninth Congress of the WPK and continuously open up new prospects for the cause of Party and state development. China and the DPRK are friendly socialist neighbors who stand by each other and share weal and woe, Xi said, stressing that it is an unswerving policy of the CPC and the Chinese government to preserve, consolidate and develop China-DPRK relations. Xi noted that in June this year, he paid a state visit to the DPRK and met with Kim again, opening a new chapter in the development of relations between the two Parties and the two countries. Xi said that he stands ready to work together with Kim to continue strengthening the strategic guidance of relations between the two Parties and the two countries, jointly promote the development of their respective Party and state causes, continuously improve the well-being of the two peoples and deepen their friendship, so as to make greater contributions to promoting peace, stability, development and prosperity in the region and the world at large.

item.title: Xi extends Teachers' Day greetings, urges nurturing capable youth for national rejuvenation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has extended greetings to teachers and educators across the country ahead of Teachers' Day, which is celebrated annually on Sept. 10. In a congratulatory message, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, called on teachers nationwide to enhance their professional competence and capabilities, and foster a new generation of young people to shoulder the mission of realizing national rejuvenation.

item.title: Taiwan has never been a country and will never be one: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 8 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Tuesday that Taiwan has never been a country and will never be a country, adding that the Lai Ching-te authorities' deliberate distortion of UNGA Resolution 2758 once again revealed their separatist nature for "Taiwan independence." Mao made the remarks at a regular news briefing when asked to comment on Lai's claim that China is contorting UNGA Resolution 2758 and that Taiwan is a "sovereign independent nation." Lai Ching-te authorities' rhetoric will not change the historical and legal fact that the two sides of the Taiwan Strait belong to one and the same China, nor will it undermine the international community's steadfast commitment to one China, she said. UNGA Resolution 2758 solemnly reaffirmed the one-China principle, which "decides to restore all its rights to the People's Republic of China and to recognize the representatives of its Government as the only legitimate representatives of China to the United Nations," she said. From political, legal and procedural aspects, the resolution resolved once and for all the question of the representation of the whole of China, including Taiwan, in the UN, she said, adding that it made clear that there is only one seat of China in the United Nations, and there is no such thing as "two Chinas" or "one China, one Taiwan."

item.title: Asian coast guard high-level meeting to address non-traditional security challenges
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
By Li Lei The upcoming 22nd Heads of Asian Coast Guard Agencies (HACGAM) High-Level Meeting will focus on non-traditional security challenges and ways to manage risks and crises amid a "complex and volatile" regional maritime security situation, a China Coast Guard spokesman said on Monday. The annual forum, set to open Tuesday in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province, will also explore effective ways to promote cross-border cooperation and safeguard maritime peace and stability, spokesman Liu Dejun said. Liu noted that the meeting has evolved over more than two decades, expanding its membership to include countries and regions across East Asia, Southeast Asia, South Asia, and even some outside the region. Its institutional framework has grown increasingly robust, while cooperation has broadened into new areas. The organizing of HACGAM meetings follows China's chairing of the North Pacific Coast Guard Forum last year — an expansion from a six-nation "North Pacific Plus" event to a broader pan-Asia-Pacific forum. Liu said China remains committed to promoting its vision of a "maritime community with a shared future" and its Global Security Initiative, aiming to build consensus on regional maritime security governance. China hosted the HACGAM working-level meeting in May in Quanzhou, Fujian province, which provided technical support and outcomes that facilitated the opening of this week's high-level session.
